Backend: 17/17 pytest passed. Frontend: 12/12 UI flows verified (bad password error message, admin login, session reload persistence, admin no amber badge, license alert banner visible with count, scheduling branch filter reduces to Karim (Plateau), payroll branch filter shows single row Karim Benali with brut 1 440,00 $ (non-breaking space), employees branch filter works, password dialog rejects wrong current with 'Mot de passe actuel incorrect.' error, logout returns to landing, superadmin (jeff) login shows amber pulse badge on sidebar-password-button, superadmin sees audit-trail-panel populated). Julie (employee) login shows myspace and no licenses link (non-regression). CRITICAL SECURITY BUG: brute-force lockout is bypassed via the public URL because request.client.host rotates across k8s ingress upstream IPs (10.208.151.74/75/...), so the identifier 'ip:email' never accumulates 5 fails; verified 7 consecutive bad logins via public URL all return 401 (never 429). Works correctly on localhost:8001 (127.0.0.1 identifier).

critical.issue: Brute force lockout uses identifier = f'{request.client.host}:{email}'. Behind the k8s ingress, request.client.host is the upstream proxy IP which rotates per request, so 5 consecutive failed logins on the same email from the same real client never trigger the 15-minute 429 lockout. Reproduced with 7 consecutive bad logins via the public URL → always 401. Fix: use email-only identifier (with optional CIDR from X-Forwarded-For's leftmost value), and rely on Mongo TTL/periodic cleanup instead of per-IP bucketing.

action_items: Change brute-force lockout identifier from 'ip:email' to 'email' (or leftmost X-Forwarded-For + email) so protection works behind the k8s ingress in production. Current code path server.py:184-197 makes the 429 branch unreachable via the public URL.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:184 — brute force identifier uses request.client.host which returns the ingress upstream IP behind kubernetes. This IP rotates so lockout never triggers via the public URL (verified). Read the leftmost X-Forwarded-For or drop the IP part.

server.py:191-197 — on the 5th failed attempt, update['count']=0 is set together with locked_until; that means the 5th call still returns 401 (not 429). Only the 6th attempt sees the lockout. Consider also raising 429 on the 5th attempt for clarity, and add a Retry-After header.
server.py:262 — resend.api_key = RESEND_API_KEY is captured once at import time; if the .env value changes, existing worker would need a restart. Move to inside send_report_email().
AuthContext.tsx:70-77 — /auth/me revalidation on mount silently signs the user out on any error (including transient network 5xx). Consider retrying once before setAuth(null) to avoid random logouts.

rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force lockout bug: FastAPI's request.client.host reflects the *immediate* TCP peer, which behind the emergent kubernetes ingress is one of several rotating upstream proxy IPs (observed: 10.208.151.74, 10.208.151.75, and others). The lockout key is f'{ip}:{email}', so each attempt lands in a different Mongo document and the count never reaches LOCKOUT_ATTEMPTS=5. Mitigation: parse the leftmost X-Forwarded-For header, or key the lockout on email alone (accept a small risk of shared-lockout DoS on a legitimate user in exchange for real BF protection). Alternatively add a small per-email counter alongside the per-IP one.
